decisions.question: Is the accessible name label + ": " + getValueLabel(...), or getValueLabel alone?
decisions.decision: getValueLabel(value, max) returns the whole text alternative. RatingDisplay has no `label` input. An aria-label or aria-labelledby that the application passes to the root wins where the adapter forwards attributes; when either is present getValueLabel is not asked for and no second aria-label is written.
decisions.reason: Rule 14 forbids the adapter joining label and value with ": ". The three framework adapters already removed `label` (verified: react expanded-controls.tsx:58-61, vue controls.ts:406-420, angular advanced-controls.ts:170); only the aria-labelledby case differs.

decisions.question: May a slide carry its own `label` that is appended to the slide and indicator names?
decisions.decision: No. A slide and its indicator are named by getSlideLabel(position, total) alone (position is one-based); the slide data has no `label` field that the adapter reads for a name. In vanilla an aria-label authored on a slide element is used as written (rule 7) and the template attribute is data-hw-slide-label="{position} / {total}".
decisions.reason: The specified signature cannot see a slide title and rule 14 forbids composing "<label>, <position of total>". All three framework adapters already name slides from getSlideLabel only (vue removed CarouselSlide.label; angular interactions.ts:132; react expanded-interactive.tsx:113).

The input is named by `label` (or aria-label / aria-labelledby / a parent Field where the adapter supports them); dropLabel is never the fallback name. dropLabel (required always) is the visible instruction:

dropLabel

placed before the input, and the input lists that id first in aria-describedby. When dropLabel is missing the paragraph is not rendered and its id is not added to aria-describedby. A missing name warns as requireText('FileDropzone', 'label', …).

Specification: "dropLabel no longer doubles as the field label: label is supplied separately". Rule 12: no fallback from another input and no empty element. React and Vue already use the class and the describedby reference; Angular renders a bare

that nothing references, and Vue renders an empty

when dropLabel is missing.

decisions.question: Is the selection status always rendered (getSelectedMessage required), or only when the application supplies getSelectedMessage?
decisions.decision:
getSelectedMessage?: (files: readonly File[]) => string is optional ("when wanted") in the framework adapters and is itself the switch: when it is supplied the adapter renders one visible

after the input (no hw-sr-only class; empty until files are selected, then the complete returned string, and empty again after a reset or a rejected selection); when it is omitted no status element is rendered and nothing warns. The adapter never lists or joins file names itself as a status. In vanilla the switch is the authored [data-hw-file-status] element, and getSelectedMessage (option or data-hw-selected-message="{count} …") is required while that element exists.
decisions.reason: Vue treated the function as the switch, Angular made it required and always rendered a visually hidden status, React rendered none. The function-as-switch form asks the least text from the application, needs no new input, and is expressible in all adapters; the styles package already styles .hw-file-dropzone [role=status] as visible muted text. The React addition is two lines.

decisions.question: Which adapters take getRejectedMessage and unsupportedDropMessage, and under which condition?
decisions.decision: getRejectedMessage(rejected: readonly File[]) is required where the adapter itself renders the rejection text: React when `accept` is set (union on accept), vanilla when [data-hw-file-status] exists and accept or data-hw-max-size/options.maxSize is set. Vue and Angular render no rejection text (they hand the files to the application through the reject event / (rejected) output) and take no such input until they do. unsupportedDropMessage stays vanilla only and is required while [data-hw-file-status] exists (it depends on the browser at run time, so rule 9 makes it "always" under that static switch). Vanilla template attributes expose {count} only; file names need the function option.
decisions.reason: The specification allows an adapter that does not render a text to take no input for it, and names unsupportedDropMessage vanilla only. Rendering a rejection message in Vue and Angular needs new error state and wiring, which is a feature (see parityGaps).

decisions.component: every component whose `label` names its root or its field (Breadcrumb, Pagination, Stepper, Spinner, Timeline, AvatarGroup, Carousel, Calendar, SecondaryNav, ContentNavigation, ToastRegion, NotificationList, TreeView, Tabs lists, DatePicker and the other field controls, FileDropzone, RatingDisplay.getValueLabel)
decisions.question: Rules 8 and 10 clash: a root or field name is "always" (rule 10: required in the type) but an aria-label, an aria-labelledby or a parent Field label satisfies it (rule 8). Which wins, per adapter?
decisions.decision: Rule 8 defines the requirement: the element must have a name from `label`, aria-label, aria-labelledby or (field controls) the parent Field label. Enforcement follows what each adapter can express. React: a union type, RootName / FieldName from packages/react/src/shared.tsx ({label} | {aria-label} | {aria-labelledby}); a missing name is a type error and text(Component, 'label', …) warns only when all are absent. Vue: these names are declared without required: true and without a default (label: String), and are enforced at run time only: requireText(Component, 'label', …) is called at render unless attrs['aria-label'], attrs['aria-labelledby'] or a parent Field label has text. Every other "always" text in Vue stays required: true. Angular: host attributes are not forwarded to the inner root, so `label` is the only source and stays @Input({required: true}). Vanilla: authored markup first (rule 7), requireText only when the markup leaves the element unnamed. DatePicker.label follows the same rule as every other field control.
decisions.reason: With required: true Vue prints "Missing required prop: label" (and vue-tsc reports an error) for <HwBreadcrumb aria-label="…">, which rule 8 and the README explicitly allow; the Vue DatePicker already had to stay optional for the documented Field composition. One rule for all names that ARIA can satisfy removes the false warning and still reports a truly unnamed component once. React already implements exactly this as a union.

perAdapter.vue: packages/vue/src: for every component that names its root through rootLabel(…) (shared.ts:58; today AvatarGroup, Calendar, Carousel, NotificationList, Timeline, Breadcrumb, ContentNavigation, Pagination, SecondaryNav, Stepper, ToastRegion) and for Spinner, TreeView and any other root whose `label` is satisfied by aria-label/aria-labelledby, change the prop from label: { type: String, required: true } to label: String. Do not change labels that are visible content (Feedback.label, CookieConsent.title, Field labels of components without attrs forwarding). DatePicker.label and FileDropzone.label stay as they are (optional, run-time checked). Document the rule once in packages/vue/README.md. Test in packages/vue/test/required-text.test.ts: mounting Breadcrumb, Pagination and Spinner with only aria-label produces no console.warn at all (neither Vue's "Missing required prop" nor Hawiyah's); mounting them with no name produces exactly one Hawiyah warning each and no aria-label attribute.

decisions.question: When is rangeLabel required on Calendar, and what is the text of the supported-range tooltip?
decisions.decision: DatePicker: rangeLabel is required always (the picker always renders the Gregorian/Hijri switch). Calendar in React, Vue and Angular: required when calendar is 'islamic-umalqura' (the only case in which the calendar renders the information control; the calendar prop is the static switch). Vanilla createCalendar renders the switch itself, so rangeLabel, calendarSystemLabel, gregorianLabel, hijriLabel and unsupportedMessage are required always there. The information control is named by rangeLabel alone (role="img", aria-label=rangeLabel, the letter "i" is not part of the name). The tooltip text is rangeLabel, one U+0020, then the ISO range "UMALQURA_MIN_DATE – UMALQURA_MAX_DATE" isolated as left-to-right data; no colon or other punctuation is added. With rangeLabel missing the tooltip holds the range alone and the control has no aria-label.
decisions.reason: The specification condition ("when the calendar-system switch is rendered") only fits vanilla; the three framework calendars render the range information themselves in Umm al-Qura mode and all three already use the calendar prop as the condition and the same space-joined text (react calendar.tsx:27,64; vue calendar.ts:259; angular advanced-controls.ts:232). Vanilla puts the label and the range in adjacent elements with no white space, so their text runs together.

perAdapter.vanilla: packages/vanilla/src/calendar.ts (lines 74-76): when rangeLabel has text, append a single space text node between infoLabel and infoRange (infoPanel.append(infoLabel, ' ', infoRange)); when it has none, append infoRange only (no empty span). Test in packages/vanilla/test/text.test.ts: the tooltip textContent equals rangeLabel + ' ' + '1924-08-01 – 2077-11-16'.

decisions.question: One signature (message: ToastMessage) => string, but vanilla toasts are authored elements.
decisions.decision: The name (getDismissLabel), the requiredness (when a message can be dismissed) and the result (the complete accessible name of the dismiss button, nothing added) are the same in all four adapters. The argument is the toast as the adapter holds it: the message object in React, Vue and Angular, and the authored toast element in vanilla ((toast: HTMLElement) => string). Vanilla source order: the dismiss button's authored aria-label or text, then data-hw-dismiss-label="… {title}" on the region, then options.getDismissLabel.
decisions.reason: Vanilla has no message data to pass, and inventing a message object would be new public API. Markup versus data is an adapter mechanism; the template placeholder {title} gives markup-only pages the same information.

decisions.question: Vanilla keeps an extra optional getStatusMessage(value) beside successMessage. Keep, remove or add everywhere?
decisions.decision: Keep it in vanilla only, optional, with no default and no warning; successMessage stays the required text in all four adapters. It is not added to React, Vue or Angular.
decisions.reason: The specification says so explicitly ("options.getStatusMessage(value) stays as an optional override with no default"). It is a vanilla mechanism, not a missing feature elsewhere: controller options are not reactive, whereas a framework application changes successMessage itself when the answer changes.

decisions.component: Combobox, MultiSelect, TagInput (requiredMessage); DatePicker (invalidMessage, unsupportedMessage, unavailableMessage)
decisions.question: Rule 13 says a constraint with a missing message keeps "a single-space custom validity and aria-invalid=true". Is aria-invalid set because a message is missing?
decisions.decision: No. A missing message changes the validation message only: the adapter sets a single-space custom validity so the constraint still blocks submission, and warns. aria-invalid is exactly what it would be with the message present: Combobox, MultiSelect and TagInput do not set it for an empty required control (they expose it only from `error` / the field state / an application attribute), and DatePicker keeps setting it for an actually invalid, unsupported or unavailable value whether or not the message exists.
decisions.reason: The parenthesis in rule 13 contradicts its own title ("Validation never depends on text") and rule 12 (behaviour stays the same; the warning is the only signal): with the message present no adapter marks an untouched empty required field invalid, so marking it only when a string is missing makes an ARIA state depend on text and announces an error on a field the user has not touched. Vanilla, Vue and Angular already behave this way; only React added it after review.

decisions.component: PortalFooter, SiteVerification, ServiceCard, Calendar tooltip, FileUploadList and every place that puts two texts side by side
decisions.question: Spoken separators (" · ", ": ", "، ") were replaced by a space in some adapters; is a literal space a forbidden fixed token, and where is it written?
decisions.decision: No adapter renders " · ", ": ", "، ", ", " or any other punctuation between application texts or between text and data (verified: none remains in packages/*/src). A single U+0020 between two inline runs is kept, because it is white space and not a word or punctuation, and without it assistive technology reads the two runs as one word. Rules: (1) the screen-reader-only externalLabel after a link is externalLabel, with the space inside the span so the visible link has no trailing space; (2) a data value after a label is written as label, one space, value (SiteVerification: domainLabel + space + domain; registrationLabel + space + registrationNumber); (3) the calendar range tooltip follows D07; (4) nothing is appended to httpsLabel; (5) decorative glyphs that carry no language (★, ×, /, –, …, +N, the letter i of the information icon) stay only inside aria-hidden elements or where a function input supplies the name.
decisions.reason: Rule 14 forbids words, language-specific punctuation and fixed tokens; a single space is neither, and all three framework adapters already converge on it. The only difference left is where Vue writes the space.

decisions.question: Do optional buttons render only while a handler is bound, and which texts does CookieConsent take?
decisions.decision: An optional action is rendered only while the application has bound its handler, and its text is required under exactly that condition: React a handler prop with a union type (handler given => label required); Vue the declared listener prop (onPreferences, onRead, onDismiss; helpers listener()/listens() in shared.ts) with an optional label prop and requireText(…, 'a <name> listener is bound'); Angular an observed output with an optional input and the same requireText condition; vanilla the authored button. A button is never rendered inert. CookieConsent takes title (always), acceptLabel (always), rejectLabel (always), preferencesLabel (when a preferences handler is bound; the button only notifies the application and does not close the banner) and policyLabel (when policyHref is set; a plain link after the description). The preferences button is the last button of the button group, data-variant="ghost".
decisions.reason: The specification conditions are "when a mark-read/dismiss handler is given" and "when the preferences action is rendered"; binding the handler is the only static switch all frameworks share, and Vue and Angular already implemented it. React lacks the preferences action and Vue lacks the policy link; each is a few lines with no new state.

decisions.question: Is the packaged action link named actionLabel + hidden title, or actionLabel alone?
decisions.decision: actionLabel alone is the whole visible text and accessible name of the packaged action link; the adapter appends nothing (no hidden title, no ": "). It is required when the card renders its own link, that is when an address is given and the application supplies no action of its own (React `action` node, Vue `action` slot, Angular projected [hwServiceAction] content). An application that wants the service name in the link puts it in actionLabel.
decisions.reason: Rule 14: an adapter does not compose an accessible name from two application texts. React and Vue rendered actionLabel alone; Angular removed its hidden suffix in the review round (verified at content.ts:62).

decisions.component: PortalLayout, DatePicker, Drawer, NavigationDrawer and every component that passes a text to an inner Hawiyah component
decisions.question: One missing text can be reported twice (once by the composite, once by the inner component). Silence it?
decisions.decision: Accepted as development-only noise, with one ordering rule: the composite calls requireText under its own name and its own input name before it delegates, so the first warning names the input the application has to set; the inner component may then report the same missing text once under its own name. No adapter adds a public input, a context or other cross-component state to suppress the second line. A module-private suppression that needs no API (the vanilla WeakSet for the calendar nested in a DatePicker) may stay.
decisions.reason: Each component must still warn for applications that use it directly (rule 11); requireText already limits every pair of component and input to one line per page. Warnings are diagnostics, not rendered output, so adapters need not match line for line.

decisions.question: Addendum A6 says the support section is rendered only with support content; Angular keeps an empty <section hidden>.
decisions.decision: Accepted for Angular. Without projected [hwFooterSupport] content the section stays in the DOM as the projection target with the `hidden` attribute, no aria-label and no heading, so it is neither displayed nor exposed to assistive technology; with content it has aria-label=supportLabel and the heading, as in React and Vue, which omit the element. supportLabel is required when support content is given, in all adapters.

The result for users and assistive technology is the same; only the inert node differs, which is an adapter mechanism.

decisions.component: Popover and Menu (triggerLabel), TagInput (addLabel), MultiSelect (getSelectedMessage, getResultsMessage), TreeView (getExpandLabel, getCollapseLabel), Feedback (commentLabel, submitLabel), Calendar system switch texts
decisions.question: Texts the specification marks "when the adapter renders …": required or optional where an adapter always renders the part?
decisions.decision: The requiredness follows what the adapter renders. Where the adapter always renders the part, the text is required always in that adapter (React required prop, Vue required: true, Angular @Input({required: true})). Where a prop, slot, handler or attribute switches the part on, it is a "when" text (React union, optional in Vue and Angular, requireText with the condition). Where the adapter does not render the part, it takes no input of that name, and the name stays reserved for the day it does.
decisions.reason: This is what the specification conditions mean and what all four adapters did; the Angular reviewer recorded the required inputs for parity tracking only. The differences that remain are missing features, listed under parityGaps.

decisions.question: emptyMessage is "always", but React and Vue Table also accept a native table as children/slot without `columns`, where no empty row exists.
decisions.decision: emptyMessage is required when `columns` is given (the static switch that makes the component render rows itself). React: union on columns (already). Vue: optional prop, requireText('Table', 'emptyMessage', …, 'columns is given') at render when columns is given. Angular hw-table always takes columns, so it stays @Input({required: true}). DataTable.emptyMessage stays required always in all adapters.
decisions.reason: Rule 9 allows "when" for a static prop switch, and demanding a text that can never be rendered contradicts rule 12. Vue required: true warns for the documented slot-only use.

README row. Test in packages/vue/test/required-text.test.ts: slot-only Table without emptyMessage logs nothing; Table with columns, no rows and no emptyMessage logs one warning and renders no empty cell text.

decisions.question: A decorative spinner (aria-hidden="true") needs no label; how is `label` typed?

Angular: `label` stays @Input({required: true}); a decorative spinner sets aria-hidden="true" on the host and passes label="", and nothing is reported. Vanilla: authored markup.

decisions.question: How do externalLabel, legalLinksLabel and supportLabel reach the footer through the layout, and is the container required?
decisions.decision: The names are those of PortalFooter in every adapter; the container follows how each adapter already passes footer content, as the specification says: React and Vue footerProps.externalLabel / legalLinksLabel / supportLabel, Angular top-level inputs of hw-portal-layout (externalLabel; legalLinksLabel and supportLabel only on hw-portal-footer because the Angular layout passes no legal links and no support content). externalLabel is required always: React types footerProps as required with a required externalLabel; Vue cannot type a nested key, so PortalLayout calls needText('PortalLayout', 'footerProps.externalLabel', …) at render (already done); Angular @Input({required: true}) externalLabel. menuLabel and navigationLabel are top-level layout inputs in all three.
decisions.reason: Explicit in the specification ("reach the footer the way each adapter already passes footer content"). No change needed.

decisions.question: Angular keeps the brand as an <a> without href when there is no home address; other adapters render a non-link element.
decisions.decision: Accepted. Addendum A5 asks that a brand without a home address has no link role and no href; an <a> without href has neither and is not focusable. The element name may differ between adapters; the class (.hw-portal-brand), the absence of href and role, and brandLabel handling may not.
decisions.reason: Adapter mechanism with the same result for users and assistive technology.

decisions.question: Addendum D: what happens when `locale` is missing? Vanilla throws (which aborts enhance() for the whole page); core now throws a TypeError when a helper is called without a locale.
decisions.decision: `locale: string` is required always in all four adapters (React required prop; Angular @Input({required: true}); Vue required: true; vanilla options.locale, else data-hw-locale on the controller root, never a `lang` attribute) and has no default anywhere. No adapter throws for a missing locale and none calls a core helper without one: before any call of getCalendarMonth or formatCalendarDate the adapter evaluates requireText('Calendar' | 'DatePicker', 'locale', locale). When it is false the component renders nothing that Intl would have produced: Calendar renders its root element with its name and attributes but no toolbar, no weekday row, no grid and no status; DatePicker renders its field, text input (which keeps the ISO value as typed; ISO dates are data), hidden input, trigger and dialog as usual, shows no formatted-date output, and its nested calendar is empty. Value, form participation and events are unchanged. The DatePicker passes its locale to the nested Calendar; the nested calendar may warn once more under its own name (D14).
decisions.reason: Addendum D2 names the requireText warning as the mechanism for a missing locale in Vue and vanilla, and rule 12 (renders nothing in its place, structure stays) is the model. A throw in one controller makes enhance() release every controller on the page. Core throws only as a backstop so that nothing can fall back to the host locale.

decisions.question: Addendum D: DataTable sorts text with core sortRows and defaulted its locale to 'ar-SA' in React, Vue and Angular (vanilla fell through to the core default).
decisions.decision: `locale: string` is a required input of DataTable with no default, under the same name in all four adapters: React required prop; Angular @Input({required: true}); Vue { type: String, required: true }; vanilla options.locale, else data-hw-locale on the controller root, required when the table has at least one [data-hw-sort] button. Every adapter evaluates requireText('DataTable', 'locale', locale) (vanilla with when = 'a column is sortable') and calls sortRows(rows, key, direction, locale) only when it is true. With the locale missing, sort state, aria-sort, the sort event and getSortLabel behave as usual, and the rows stay in their source order. Numbers in cells are rendered as given; the adapter formats nothing.
decisions.reason: Addendum D2 and D4: required input with one name, a type error in React and Angular, a warning in Vue and vanilla, and unchanged output when the application passes the former default. Sortable columns are data, so rule 9 makes the requirement "always" in the frameworks; in vanilla the sort buttons are authored markup, a static switch.

decisions.question: Addendum D: the vanilla RangeSlider writes "a – b" into [data-hw-range-output] with core formatNumber and no locale of its own.
decisions.decision: Vanilla: `locale` (options.locale, else data-hw-locale on the controller root) is required when the root contains a [data-hw-range-output] element. With a locale the output text is formatNumber(lower, {locale}) + " – " + formatNumber(upper, {locale}) as today (the en dash is a glyph); without one the controller calls requireText('RangeSlider', 'locale', locale, 'a [data-hw-range-output] element is present'), does not call formatNumber and leaves the output empty. Thumb values, clamping and events are unchanged. React keeps its application formatter formatValue (default String, which chooses no locale); Vue and Angular render no formatted value and take no locale.
decisions.reason: Addendum D2: a component that formats a number takes a required locale whenever that feature is used, or a formatter from the application where one already exists (React). The output element is authored markup, a static switch.

decisions.question: Addendum D: only the Vue Stat formats a numeric value (formatNumber with a default 'ar-SA' locale prop); React and Angular render `value` as given and vanilla is authored markup.
decisions.decision: Stat renders `value` exactly as the application gives it in every adapter and takes no `locale`. The Vue-only number formatting and its `locale` prop are removed; an application that wants grouping formats the number itself (core formatNumber(value, { locale })) and passes the string.
decisions.reason: Same input names and the same rendered result in all four adapters with no new public API; adding a locale input to React and Angular for a Vue-only convenience would be a new feature. Breaking for Vue: a number such as 1234567 is now printed without grouping.

ownerQuestions.question: core formatDate keeps timeZone = 'Asia/Riyadh' and calendar = 'gregory' as defaults, and getCalendarMonth takes "today" in Asia/Riyadh. They are not locale choices, but they are a regional default inside an otherwise neutral package. Keep, or make the time zone a required argument too?
ownerQuestions.recommendation: Keep for 0.3.0 and document it (done in CONTRACT.md and packages/core/README.md): the calendar is defined for Saudi civil use, the Umm al-Qura day boundary is a Riyadh boundary, and an explicit timeZone already overrides it. Revisit before 1.0 together with a `today`/`timeZone` option on getCalendarMonth, because a host-zone default would be worse (server and client could disagree).

ownerQuestions.question: Intl itself falls back to the locale of the host when the application passes a well-formed tag the runtime has no data for (for example "xx-YY"). Should core detect this (Intl.*.supportedLocalesOf) and warn or throw?
ownerQuestions.recommendation: Do not throw. The application chose the tag, and data availability belongs to the runtime. If wanted, add a development-only warning in a later step; it is not part of addendum D.

ownerQuestions.question: Rule 13 text: D10 decides that aria-invalid is not set merely because a validation message is missing. Should the controls that use a custom required validity (Combobox, MultiSelect, TagInput) expose aria-invalid="true" after a failed submission attempt (the invalid event), with or without a message?
ownerQuestions.recommendation: Yes, in milestone 3, in all four adapters at once and independent of the text; then reword rule 13 to "the control stays invalid and blocks submission". Until then no adapter sets it.

ownerQuestions.question: D25 removes number formatting from the Vue Stat (1234567 is printed without grouping unless the application formats it). Accept this breaking change?
ownerQuestions.recommendation: Accept and list it in the 0.3.0 migration notes. The alternative (an optional locale input on Stat in all adapters, formatting only when supplied) is a new feature for three adapters and can follow later.

ownerQuestions.question: D23 makes DataTable.locale required even for a table that has no sortable column (React, Vue, Angular), because sortable columns are data.
ownerQuestions.recommendation: Accept: DataTable exists for sorting (plain tables use Table), and addendum D4 asks for a type error. The alternative is an optional input that warns only when a column is sortable, which loses the type error.

ownerQuestions.question: D08 keeps the vanilla getDismissLabel argument as the toast element, which differs from the specified (message: ToastMessage) signature.
ownerQuestions.recommendation: Accept as an adapter mechanism (authored markup versus data). If one shared label function across adapters matters, a later step can pass { id, title, element } in vanilla; that adds a public type.

ownerQuestions.question: TreeView: which is the reference behaviour, the toggle exposed as a named button (React, Vue; needs getExpandLabel/getCollapseLabel) or hidden from assistive technology (Angular)?
ownerQuestions.recommendation: Take the exposed toggle as the reference: touch screen-reader users cannot press arrow keys, and activating the treeitem selects instead of expanding. Bring Angular to it in milestone 3; it then takes the two function inputs as required.

ownerQuestions.question: Carousel: should slide names be able to include a slide title (getSlideLabel(position, total, slide))? D02 keeps (position, total).
ownerQuestions.recommendation: No change. A slide title is visible content of the slide; the name "position of total" is what the pattern needs. Extending the signature later is additive.

ownerQuestions.question: Scripts that do not separate words with spaces (Chinese, Japanese, Thai): D11 keeps one U+0020 between a link text and its screen-reader-only externalLabel and between a label and a data value.
ownerQuestions.recommendation: Keep. The space is not visible in the first case, and in the second it separates text from data (a domain name, a number), where a space is correct in every script.

ownerQuestions.question: Angular host attributes: should the Angular wrappers forward aria-label / aria-labelledby to the inner root so that rule 8 holds there too?
ownerQuestions.recommendation: Yes, in milestone 3 as a parity fix (it changes the public surface of many components); until then `label` is the only source in Angular and is documented as such.
